claim: Ripply2 directly binds to Tbx6 in cultured cells without changing the stability of Tbx6.
source: Here, we show that Ripply2 directly binds to Tbx6 in cultured cells without changing the stability of Tbx6, indicating an unknown mechanism for Tbx6 degradation in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 1A and 1B, demonstrating direct interaction between Ripply2 and Tbx6 in cultured cells.

claim: Tbx6 degradation via Ripply2 was successfully reproduced using a mouse ES induction system.
source: We succeeded in reproducing in vivo events using a mouse ES induction system, in which Tbx6 degradation occurred via Ripply2.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing Tbx6-venus degradation upon Ripply2 induction in PSM-fated ES cells, as shown in Figure 2.

claim: Proteasomes are major components of the Ripply2-binding complex in PSM-fated ES cells.
source: Mass spectrometry analysis of the PSM-fated ES cells revealed that proteasomes are major components of the Ripply2-binding complex, suggesting that recruitment of a protein-degradation-complex is a pivotal function of Ripply2.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data identifying all 26S proteasome subunits as Ripply2-interacting proteins, as shown in Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: A motif in the T-box (amino acids 124-152) is required for Tbx6 degradation independent of binding with Ripply2 in vivo.
source: Finally, we identified a motif in the T-box, which is required for Tbx6 degradation independent of binding with Ripply2 in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by BAC transgenic and chimera experiments showing that deletion of amino acids 124-152 stabilizes Tbx6 protein without disrupting Ripply2 binding, as shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Tbx6 maintains the mesodermal properties of somite progenitor cells.
source: Tbx6 maintains the mesodermal properties of somite progenitor cells (Chapman and Papaioannou, 1998), but induces the expression of segmentation genes in the anterior PSM to establish the new somite boundary (Oginuma et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Chapman and Papaioannou, 1998.

claim: Tbx6 induces the expression of segmentation genes in the anterior PSM to establish the new somite boundary.
source: Tbx6 maintains the mesodermal properties of somite progenitor cells (Chapman and Papaioannou, 1998), but induces the expression of segmentation genes in the anterior PSM to establish the new somite boundary (Oginuma et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Oginuma et al., 2008.

claim: The segmentation clock periodicity is translated into the activation of the segmentation gene Mesp2 around the segmental border.
source: The periodicity of this segmentation clock is translated into the activation of the segmentation gene Mesoderm posterior protein 2 (Mesp2) around the segmental border (Morimoto et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Morimoto et al., 2005.

claim: Mesp2 expression is temporally regulated by Notch signaling and spatially defined by Tbx6.
source: Mesp2 expression is temporally regulated by Notch signaling, and spatially defined by Tbx6; both factors work positively and coordinate each other (Yasuhiko et al., 2006; Yasuhiko et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Yasuhiko et al., 2006 and 2008.

claim: The anterior limit of the Mesp2 mRNA expression domain is consistent with the Tbx6 anterior limit.
source: The anterior limit of the Mesp2 mRNA expression domain is consistent with the Tbx6 anterior limit.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the spatial relationship between Mesp2 and Tbx6 expression domains.

claim: Mesp2 induces the expression of Ripply2, which then suppresses Tbx6 protein, resulting in the termination of Mesp2 transcription.
source: Once translated, Mesp2 induces the expression of its target gene Ripply2, then Ripply2 suppresses Tbx6 protein, which results in the termination of Mesp2 transcription (Oginuma et al., 2008; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Oginuma et al., 2008 and Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Zebrafish ripply1/2 and mouse Ripply2 proteins play a role in the degradation of T-box family factors.
source: Recently, both zebrafish ripply1/2 and mouse Ripply2 proteins were found to play a role in the degradation of T-box family factors (Wanglar et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Wanglar et al., 2014 and Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Ectopic Ripply2 expression in the posterior PSM is sufficient for the destabilization of Tbx6 and T protein.
source: Our previous study demonstrated that ectopic Ripply2 expression in the posterior PSM was sufficient for the destabilization of T-box factors- Tbx6 and T protein (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: FLAG-Tbx6 strongly associates with Myc-Ripply2 in HEK293T cell lysates.
source: A strong association between FLAG-Tbx6 with Myc-Ripply2 was observed with HEK293T cell lysates (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Tbx6 directly interacts with Ripply2 as demonstrated by GST pull-down assay.
source: GST-Tbx6 fusion protein, but not GST alone, was able to pull down His-Ripply2, indicating that Tbx6 directly interacts with Ripply2 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The T-box domain alone is sufficient for association with Ripply2.
source: We found that the T-box domain alone was sufficient for association with Ripply2 and that other regions of Tbx6 were dispensable for this interaction (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data with various Tbx6 deletion constructs shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ripply2ΔFPIQ mutant lacks the ability to bind Tbx6.
source: We found that both these mutants lacked the ability to bind Tbx6 (Figure 1D), indicating that these conserved sequences are required for Ripply2-mediated Tbx6 suppression.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data with Ripply2 mutants shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ripply2ΔWRPW mutant lacks the ability to bind Tbx6.
source: We found that both these mutants lacked the ability to bind Tbx6 (Figure 1D), indicating that these conserved sequences are required for Ripply2-mediated Tbx6 suppression.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data with Ripply2 mutants shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The transcriptional activity of mouse Tbx6 is not influenced by mouse Ripply2 and TLE1.
source: However, the transcriptional activity of mouse Tbx6 was not influenced by mouse Ripply2 and TLE1 (homolog of Groucho in mouse) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tbx6 was never destabilized in HEK293T cells even in the presence of Ripply2.
source: Despite Tbx6-Ripply2 interaction, Tbx6 was never destabilized in HEK293T cells even in the presence of Ripply2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1A showing stable Tbx6 levels despite Ripply2 co-expression.

claim: Ectopic expression of Ripply2 in the cardiac mesoderm does not influence the stability of T-box factors Tbx18 and Tbx5 in the heart.
source: In addition, the ectopic expression of Ripply2 in the cardiac mesoderm did not influence on the stability of T-box factors Tbx18 and Tbx5 in the heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), which is different from the destabilizing effect of Ripply2 on Tbx6 and Brachyury (T) in the PSM.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The PSM contains a specific factor(s) necessary for the destabilization of T-box factors.
source: These results suggest that the PSM contains a specific factor(s) necessary for the destabilization of T-box factors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tbx6 degradation occurs in PSM tissue but not in cultured cells or other tissues.

claim: ES cells cultured with CHIR99021 exhibited Tbx6-venus expression from day 2 to day 4.
source: Compared with ES cells treated with DMSO that exhibited almost no venus-positive cells, ES cells cultured with CHIR99021 exhibited Tbx6-venus expression from day 2 to day 4, as indicated by immunostaining with anti-GFP antibody (Figure 1G–R).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1G-R.

claim: The expression of Tbx6-venus peaked at day 3 of PSM induction.
source: The expression of Tbx6-venus peaked at day 3 (Figure 1P) and was maintained until day 4 (Figure 1R).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1P and 1R.

claim: The expression level of FLAG-Ripply2 reached the peak at 6 hr after induction by Dox in PSM-fated differentiating ES cells.
source: In PSM-fated differentiating ES cells, we found that the expression level of FLAG-Ripply2 reached the peak at 6 hr after induction by Dox (Figure 2D), along with a gradual decrease in Tbx6-venus expression from 3 to 12 hr after Dox treatment (Figure 2D and E–N, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Tbx6-venus expression gradually decreased from 3 to 12 hr after Dox treatment in PSM-fated ES cells.
source: In PSM-fated differentiating ES cells, we found that the expression level of FLAG-Ripply2 reached the peak at 6 hr after induction by Dox (Figure 2D), along with a gradual decrease in Tbx6-venus expression from 3 to 12 hr after Dox treatment (Figure 2D and E–N, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and immunostaining data shown in Figure 2D, E-N, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-L.

claim: Ripply2-dependent reduction in Tbx6 protein was suppressed by the inclusion of 10 μM MG132.
source: This Ripply2-dependent reduction in Tbx6 protein was suppressed by the inclusion of 10 μM MG132 (a proteasome inhibitor) (Figure 2O–S, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), and some Ripply2-Tbx6 double-positive cells were observed under the Dox+MG132+ conditions (arrows in Figure 2S').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2O-S and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Tbx6 destabilization occurs through the proteasome-mediated degradation pathway.
source: These data support the idea that Tbx6 destabilization occurred through the proteasome-mediated degradation pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that MG132, a proteasome inhibitor, prevents Tbx6 degradation.

claim: Ubiquitinated Tbx6 was detected in the presence of MG132.
source: We found several bands with higher molecular weight than FLAG-Tbx6 in the presence of MG132, and the intensity became lower in the presence of Ripply2 (Figure 2U), suggesting that these bands were ubiquitinated Tbx6.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 2U.

claim: Ubiquitinated proteins, likely including Tbx6, were observed only in the presence of MG132.
source: Ubiquitinated proteins, likely including Tbx6, were observed only in the presence of MG132.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data showing ubiquitinated proteins only when MG132 is present.

claim: Tbx6 can be ubiquitinated even in the absence of Ripply2 in PSM-fated cells.
source: These results indicate that Tbx6 can be ubiquitinated even in the absence of Ripply2 in PSM-fated cells and Ripply2 is mainly involved in the degradation step.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2U and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ripply2 is mainly involved in the degradation step of Tbx6, not the ubiquitination step.
source: These results indicate that Tbx6 can be ubiquitinated even in the absence of Ripply2 in PSM-fated cells and Ripply2 is mainly involved in the degradation step.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tbx6 ubiquitination occurs without Ripply2, but degradation requires Ripply2.

claim: The level of Tbx6 ubiquitination increased when ES cells were induced to PSM.
source: Although ubiquitinated Tbx6 was detected even in undifferentiated ES cells, the level of ubiquitination was found to be increased when ES cells were induced to PSM (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: No anterior expansion of Tbx6 expression was observed in Smurf1/2-dKO embryos.
source: However, we did not observe any anterior expansion of Tbx6 expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Tbx6 degradation did not occur in Tbx6Tbx6-venus/Tbx6-venus;mcherry-T2A-FLAG-Ripply2ΔFPIQ ES cells.
source: As expected from our binding analysis demonstrating that the Tbx6-Ripply2ΔFPIQ interaction was disrupted in HEK293T cultured cells (Figure 1D), Tbx6 degradation did not occur in the Tbx6Tbx6-venus/Tbx6-venus;mcherry-T2A-FLAG-Ripply2ΔFPIQ ES cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There is no interaction between Tbx6 and Ripply2ΔFPIQ in PSM-fated ES cells.
source: We also confirmed no interaction of Tbx6 and Ripply2ΔFPIQ in PSM-fated ES cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ripply2ΔWRPW failed to interact with Tbx6 in PSM-fated ES cells.
source: The Ripply2 mutant lacking another conserved motif, WRPW, which is required for interaction with the Groucho transcriptional co-repressors TLE1 and TLE2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), also failed to interact with Tbx6 in cultured cells (Figure 1D) and ES cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Tbx6 degradation was inhibited by Ripply2ΔWRPW in PSM-fated ES cells.
source: As such thereby Tbx6 degradation was also inhibited in PSM-fated ES cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Degradation of Tbx6 protein depends on the accessibility of Ripply2.
source: These observations support the idea that degradation of Tbx6 protein depends on the accessibility of Ripply2.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Ripply2 mutants unable to bind Tbx6 cannot induce its degradation.

claim: Ripply2 recruited all subunit components of the 26S proteasome according to mass spectrometry.
source: According to mass spectrometry, Ripply2 recruited all subunit components of the 26S proteasome (Figure 4D; Supplementary file 1), which is known as the main pathway for the degradation of nuclear proteins (von Mikecz, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The 26S proteasome is the main pathway for the degradation of nuclear proteins.
source: According to mass spectrometry, Ripply2 recruited all subunit components of the 26S proteasome (Figure 4D; Supplementary file 1), which is known as the main pathway for the degradation of nuclear proteins (von Mikecz, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by von Mikecz, 2006.

claim: Ripply2 assembled the endogenous proteasome 20S subunit regardless of differentiation induction.
source: The immunoprecipitation data showed that Ripply2 assembled the endogenous proteasome 20S subunit regardless of differentiation induction (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The function of Ripply2 for specific protein degradation is mediated through the proteasome pathway.
source: These results further support our idea that the function of Ripply2 for specific protein degradation is mediated through the proteasome pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the mass spectrometry and immunoprecipitation data showing Ripply2 interaction with proteasome components.

claim: Venus protein expressed under the control of the Tbx6 promoter was stable and expanded to the anterior region beyond the segmentation point.
source: We dissected embryos at E10.5, and confirmed that the expression of venus protein was stable and expanded to the anterior region beyond the segmentation point indicated by the arrow (N = 3. Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Tbx6-venus fusion protein faithfully reproduced the endogenous expression pattern of Tbx6 with a clear anterior border.
source: As expected, the transgene faithfully reproduced the endogenous expression pattern of Tbx6, in which the expression domain has a clear anterior border just before the segmental border in the anterior PSM (N = 3, Figure 5C), indicating that the Tbx6-fusion protein was degraded in the anterior PSM.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Tbx6ΔC-venus protein exhibited an expression pattern with a clear anterior border.
source: Tbx6ΔC-venus protein exhibited an expression pattern with a clear anterior border (N = 4, Figure 5D); however, the Tbx6ΔTC-venus protein expanded to the anterior region (N = 2, Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Tbx6ΔTC-venus protein expanded to the anterior region.
source: Tbx6ΔC-venus protein exhibited an expression pattern with a clear anterior border (N = 4, Figure 5D); however, the Tbx6ΔTC-venus protein expanded to the anterior region (N = 2, Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The T-box domain is necessary for degradation of Tbx6 protein.
source: These results indicated that the T-box domain is necessary for degradation of Tbx6 protein.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that deletion of the T-box domain prevents Tbx6 degradation.

claim: The expression of T-box-venus protein had a clear anterior border.
source: Interestingly, the expression of T-box-venus protein had a clear anterior border (N = 5, Figure 5F), demonstrating that the T-box region of Tbx6 is necessary and sufficient for degradation.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The T-box region of Tbx6 is necessary and sufficient for degradation.
source: Interestingly, the expression of T-box-venus protein had a clear anterior border (N = 5, Figure 5F), demonstrating that the T-box region of Tbx6 is necessary and sufficient for degradation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the T-box domain alone is sufficient to confer degradation properties.

claim: Degradation occurred when the T-box was partially deleted until the 152nd amino acid.
source: Using the same method, we further found that the degradation occurred when the T-box was partially deleted until the 152th amino acid (aa) (Figure 5A,H, N = 4), but not when it was deleted up to the 124th aa (Figure 5A,G, N = 2), suggesting that the 124∼152 aa region may be essential for Tbx6 degradation in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Degradation did not occur when the T-box was deleted up to the 124th amino acid.
source: Using the same method, we further found that the degradation occurred when the T-box was partially deleted until the 152th amino acid (aa) (Figure 5A,H, N = 4), but not when it was deleted up to the 124th aa (Figure 5A,G, N = 2), suggesting that the 124∼152 aa region may be essential for Tbx6 degradation in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from BAC transgenic embryos shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The 124-152 aa region may be essential for Tbx6 degradation in vivo.
source: Using the same method, we further found that the degradation occurred when the T-box was partially deleted until the 152th amino acid (aa) (Figure 5A,H, N = 4), but not when it was deleted up to the 124th aa (Figure 5A,G, N = 2), suggesting that the 124∼152 aa region may be essential for Tbx6 degradation in vivo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential degradation patterns observed with different T-box deletions.

claim: Tbx6-venus signal in chimera embryos with Tbx6Tbx6(Δ124-152aa)-venus/+ ES cells became stabilized and expanded anteriorly.
source: Intriguingly, the Tbx6-venus signal in the chimera with Tbx6Tbx6(Δ124-152aa)-venus/+ ES cells became stabilized and expanded anteriorly (N = 20, Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data from chimera embryos shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Endogenous Tbx6 but not mutant Tbx6 protein was degraded by Ripply2 in the chimera embryos.
source: We confirmed that Tbx6-venus in chimera embryo with Tbx6Tbx6(Δ124-152aa)-venus/+ ES cells had an expanded pattern (Figure 6E), whereas endogenous Tbx6 showed a clear anterior limit that was at the same position as the posterior expression domain of Ripply2 (Figure 6E–H), indicating that endogenous Tbx6 but not mutant Tbx6 protein was degraded by Ripply2 in the chimera embryos.
evidence: The claim is supported by whole-mount triple-immunostaining data shown in Figure 6E-H.

claim: The T-box, especially the aa125-152 domain, plays a central role in the degradation of Tbx6 protein in vivo.
source: These observations demonstrated that the T-box, especially the aa125∼152 domain, plays a central role in the degradation of Tbx6 protein in vivo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the chimera and BAC transgenic experiments showing that this region is required for degradation.

claim: Tbx61~124aa failed to bind Ripply2.
source: As expected, when the C-terminal from the 124th amino acid was deleted from Tbx6 (Tbx61~124aa), the mutant protein failed to bind Ripply2 (Figure 6I–J), but Tbx61~152aa succeeded in interacting with Ripply2 (Figure 6I–J), suggesting that amino acids 125 ~ 152 contain the Ripply2-binding-motif in the T-box.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Tbx61~152aa succeeded in interacting with Ripply2.
source: As expected, when the C-terminal from the 124th amino acid was deleted from Tbx6 (Tbx61~124aa), the mutant protein failed to bind Ripply2 (Figure 6I–J), but Tbx61~152aa succeeded in interacting with Ripply2 (Figure 6I–J), suggesting that amino acids 125 ~ 152 contain the Ripply2-binding-motif in the T-box.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Amino acids 125-152 contain the Ripply2-binding-motif in the T-box.
source: As expected, when the C-terminal from the 124th amino acid was deleted from Tbx6 (Tbx61~124aa), the mutant protein failed to bind Ripply2 (Figure 6I–J), but Tbx61~152aa succeeded in interacting with Ripply2 (Figure 6I–J), suggesting that amino acids 125 ~ 152 contain the Ripply2-binding-motif in the T-box.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential binding patterns observed with different T-box deletions.

claim: The deletion of 125-152 aa (Tbx6Δ124~152) did not affect the ability to form a complex with Ripply2.
source: However, we surprisingly found that the deletion of 125 ~ 152 aa (Tbx6Δ124~152) did not affect the ability to form a complex with Ripply2 either in HEK293T immunoprecipitation analysis or in GST-pull-down assay (Figure 6I–K), suggesting that although 125 ~ 152 aa has Ripply2-binding ability it is not the only Ripply2-binding motif in the T-box.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and GST pull-down data shown in Figure 6J and 6K.

claim: Although 125-152 aa has Ripply2-binding ability, it is not the only Ripply2-binding motif in the T-box.
source: However, we surprisingly found that the deletion of 125 ~ 152 aa (Tbx6Δ124~152) did not affect the ability to form a complex with Ripply2 either in HEK293T immunoprecipitation analysis or in GST-pull-down assay (Figure 6I–K), suggesting that although 125 ~ 152 aa has Ripply2-binding ability it is not the only Ripply2-binding motif in the T-box.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tbx6Δ124-152 can still bind Ripply2.

claim: The stabilization of Tbx6Δ124-152aa-venus in the chimera embryo was not due to disruption of Ripply2 association but perhaps to a special motif for degradation in the region of 125-152 aa.
source: Therefore, the stabilization of Tbx6Δ124-152aa-venus in the chimera embryo was not due to disruption of Ripply2 association but perhaps to a special motif for degradation in the region of 125 ~ 152 aa.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tbx6Δ124-152 can bind Ripply2 but is not degraded.

claim: Ripply2 physically associates with the proteasome and targets Tbx6 protein to the proteasome for permanent inactivation by degradation.
source: Proteomic screening of Ripply2-binding proteins from PSM-fated mouse ES cells identified all members of 26S proteasome subunits, and Ripply2-Tbx6 was able to form a complex through direct interaction, demonstrating that Ripply2 physically associates with the proteasome anβd targets Tbx6 protein to the proteasome for permanent inactivation by degradation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the mass spectrometry data showing Ripply2 interaction with proteasome components and the observation that Tbx6 degradation is proteasome-dependent.

claim: Ripply2-mediated Tbx6 degradation was interrupted by the proteasome inhibitor MG132.
source: Ripply2-mediated Tbx6 degradation was interrupted by the proteasome inhibitor MG132.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2O-S and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Tbx6 expression domain was elongated by one-somite-length with MG132 treatment for 2 hr in vivo.
source: This result is in agreement with the in vivo discovery that the Tbx6 expression domain was elongated by one-somite-length with MG132 treatment for 2 hr (Oginuma et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Oginuma et al., 2008.

claim: TLE1/2 are well-known Groucho family co-repressors and their expression was observed in mouse PSM tissue.
source: Although TLE1/2 are well-known Groucho family co-repressors and their expression was observed in mouse PSM tissue, mouse Tbx6 transcriptional activity was never affected when TLE1 and Ripply2 were co-transfected in an Mesp2 luciferase reporter system (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about TLE1/2 and observation of their expression in PSM tissue.

claim: The Groucho-binding motif of Ripply2 is required for binding to Tbx6.
source: We found that the Groucho-binding motif of Ripply2 is also required for binding to Tbx6, indicating that TLE1/2 may participate in the degradation of Tbx6 via protein-protein interaction.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 3C.

claim: TLE1/2 may participate in the degradation of Tbx6 via protein-protein interaction.
source: We found that the Groucho-binding motif of Ripply2 is also required for binding to Tbx6, indicating that TLE1/2 may participate in the degradation of Tbx6 via protein-protein interaction.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observation that the WRPW motif (which binds TLE) is required for Tbx6 binding.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis revealed TLE in the Ripply2-Tbx6 complex.
source: Mass spectrometry analysis also revealed TLE in the Ripply2-Tbx6 complex, possibly reflecting the involvement of TLE in Tbx6 degradation in the PSM, but its molecular function in protein degradation remains unclear.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Ripply2 can recruit the 26S proteasome subunit in ES cells without PSM-induction.
source: It is of note that Ripply2 can recruit the 26S proteasome subunit in ES cells without PSM-induction (Figure 3E), even though the Ripply2-mediated T-box factor degradation was found to be a highly context-dependent event.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Ripply2-mediated T-box factor degradation is a highly context-dependent event.
source: It is of note that Ripply2 can recruit the 26S proteasome subunit in ES cells without PSM-induction (Figure 3E), even though the Ripply2-mediated T-box factor degradation was found to be a highly context-dependent event.
evidence: The claim is based on observations that Tbx6 degradation occurs only in PSM tissue and not in other contexts.

claim: There are other factor(s), possibly cell-specific E3 ligases, that help to down-regulate Tbx6 in PSM tissue.
source: This suggests that other than proteasomes, there are other factor(s), possibly cell-specific E3 ligases, that help to down-regulate Tbx6 in PSM tissue.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that Tbx6 degradation is context-dependent and requires PSM-specific factors.

claim: A PSM-specific E3 ligase must be induced and functions in Tbx6 ubiquitination.
source: This suggests that Ripply2 is not involved in the ubiquitination step and only in the degradation step of Tbx6, indicating that a PSM-specific E3 ligase must be induced and functions in Tbx6 ubiquitination.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that Tbx6 ubiquitination increases in PSM-fated cells even without Ripply2.

claim: The T-box spans 180-200 amino acid residues.
source: The T-box, which spans 180–200 amino acid residues, is a relatively large domain for the requirement of well-known DNA binding functions, suggesting that other functions likely depend on the T-box.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the T-box domain structure.

claim: The T-box domain was confirmed to be necessary and sufficient for both Ripply2-binding and Tbx6 degradation.
source: In our study, the T-box domain was confirmed to be necessary and sufficient for both Ripply2-binding and Tbx6 degradation.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from Figures 1C, 5, and 6.

claim: T (Brachyury) has been found to be degraded by Ripply2.
source: Besides Tbx6, other T-box family transcriptional factors, such as T (Brachyury), have also been found to be degraded by Ripply2 (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Zhao et al., 2015.

claim: Zebrafish tbx6 protein has been reported to be destabilized via ripply1/2 expression.
source: Zebrafish tbx6 protein has been reported to be destabilized via ripply1/2 expression (Wanglar et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Wanglar et al., 2014.

claim: The T-box dependent degradation pathway is conserved among T-box family factors.
source: These studies support the idea that the T-box dependent degradation pathway is conserved among T-box family factors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations that multiple T-box factors are degraded via Ripply proteins across species.

claim: The domain of 124-152 aa in the T-box was found to be necessary for Tbx6 degradation in chimera mouse experiments.
source: The domain of 124 ~ 152 aa in the T-box was found to be necessary for Tbx6 degradation in our chimera mouse experiment.
evidence: The claim is supported by chimera experiment data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Tbx6Δ124-152 did not lose its ability to bind Ripply2.
source: However, Tbx6Δ124-152 did not lose its ability to bind Ripply2, indicating that this region regulates degradation not by Ripply2-Tbx6 interaction but through providing a critical protein degradation point, such as a ubiquitin-binding site.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and GST pull-down data shown in Figure 6J and 6K.

claim: The 124-152 aa region regulates degradation through providing a critical protein degradation point, such as a ubiquitin-binding site.
source: However, Tbx6Δ124-152 did not lose its ability to bind Ripply2, indicating that this region regulates degradation not by Ripply2-Tbx6 interaction but through providing a critical protein degradation point, such as a ubiquitin-binding site.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that this region is required for degradation but not for Ripply2 binding.

claim: No lysine residue or ubiquitin-binding domain was found in the 124-152 aa region.
source: However, no lysine residue or ubiquitin-binding domain was found in the 124 ~ 152 aa region.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis of the 124-152 aa region.

claim: The 124-152 aa T-box region likely contains an unusual ubiquitylation site or a specific factor may be required for the degradation of T-box factors.
source: This means that this T-box region likely contains an unusual ubiquitylation site or a specific factor may be required for the degradation of T-box factors.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that this region is required for degradation but lacks typical ubiquitination sites.

claim: Somites form periodically from the anterior end of the PSM toward the posterior direction every 2 hr.
source: During somitogenesis, somites form periodically from the anterior end of the PSM toward the posterior direction every 2 hr, which coordinates a balance between maintenance of the PSM and differentiation of epithelial somites.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about somitogenesis timing.

claim: The expression of Tbx6 starts from the progenitors of the posterior mesoderm and extends to the anterior part of presomitic mesoderm (PSM).
source: The expression of Tbx6 starts from the progenitors of the posterior mesoderm and extends to the anterior part of presomitic mesoderm (PSM), then progressively regresses from the anterior edge of its expression domain when a new somite is formed.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Tbx6 expression dynamics.

claim: Tbx6 expression progressively regresses from the anterior edge of its expression domain when a new somite is formed.
source: The expression of Tbx6 starts from the progenitors of the posterior mesoderm and extends to the anterior part of presomitic mesoderm (PSM), then progressively regresses from the anterior edge of its expression domain when a new somite is formed.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Tbx6 expression dynamics during somitogenesis.

claim: The temporal periodicity of somitogenesis is established in the posterior PSM via the function of a molecular clock.
source: The temporal periodicity of somitogenesis is established in the posterior PSM via the function of a so-called molecular clock, which is operated by complex gene regulatory networks under the control of three major signaling pathways, Notch, FGF and Wnt (Hubaud and Pourquié, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Hubaud and Pourquié, 2014.

claim: The molecular clock is operated by complex gene regulatory networks under the control of three major signaling pathways: Notch, FGF and Wnt.
source: The temporal periodicity of somitogenesis is established in the posterior PSM via the function of a so-called molecular clock, which is operated by complex gene regulatory networks under the control of three major signaling pathways, Notch, FGF and Wnt (Hubaud and Pourquié, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Hubaud and Pourquié, 2014.

claim: The Tbx6-Mesp2-Ripply2 reciprocal regulation successively defines the position of the next anterior border of Mesp2.
source: This Tbx6-Mesp2-Ripply2 reciprocal regulation is the spatial mechanism that successively defines the position of the next anterior border of Mesp2, by which the metronomic segmented somites with determined size are correctly generated (Morimoto et al., 2007; Takahashi et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Morimoto et al., 2007 and Takahashi et al., 2010.

claim: The negative feedback loop of Ripply2-Tbx6 for the termination of Mesp2 activity during each somitic cycle is the fundamental process to create the spatial periodicity of the segmented somites in mice.
source: The negative feedback loop of Ripply2-Tbx6 for the termination of Mesp2 activity during each somitic cycle is the fundamental process to create the spatial periodicity of the segmented somites in mice.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the regulatory mechanism of somitogenesis.

claim: The segmentation boundary is defined by the Tbx6 expression domain, whose anterior limit is determined by Tbx6 protein destabilization via Ripply2.
source: The segmentation boundary is defined by the Tbx6 expression domain, whose anterior limit is determined by Tbx6 protein destabilization via Ripply2.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the role of Ripply2 in defining segment borders.

claim: The population of Ripply2+ cells in the PSM is very low (only approximately 1000-3000 cells/embryo, depending on somitic phases).
source: However, it is difficult to use PSM tissue from embryos for biochemical analyses because the population of Ripply2+ cells in the PSM is very low (only approximately 1000 ~ 3000 cells/embryo, depending on somitic phases).
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge about the limited number of Ripply2-expressing cells in the PSM.

claim: Zebrafish and Xenopus ripply family factors interact with the T-box domain.
source: We presumed that Ripply2 and Tbx6 interacted directly, as reported for Zebrafish and Xenopus (Hitachi et al., 2009; Kawamura et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Hitachi et al., 2009 and Kawamura et al., 2008.

claim: The Ripply homology domain (amino acids FPIQ) is implicated in interaction with the T-box domain.
source: The presence of a so-called Ripply homology domain (amino acids FPIQ), implicated in interaction with the T-box domain (Kawamura et al., 2008), suggested that mouse Ripply2 also has the ability to bind Tbx6.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Kawamura et al., 2008.

claim: In zebrafish and Xenopus, ripply family factors repress mesp by suppressing the transcriptional activity of tbx6 as a transcriptional-repressor together with the Groucho co-repressor.
source: In zebrafish and Xenopus, ripply family factors repress mesp by suppressing the transcriptional activity of tbx6 as a transcriptional-repressor together with the Groucho co-repressor (Kawamura et al., 2005; Kawamura et al., 2008; Kondow et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Kawamura et al., 2005, 2008 and Kondow et al., 2007.

claim: Zebrafish tbx6 directly induces the expression of ripply without mediating mesp function.
source: Zebrafish tbx6 directly induces the expression of ripply without mediating mesp function, after which ripply1/2 in turn suppresses the expression of both tbx6 and mesp (Wanglar et al., 2014; Windner et al., 2015; Yabe et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Wanglar et al., 2014, Windner et al., 2015, and Yabe et al., 2016.

claim: Mouse Ripply2 requires Mesp2 for transcriptional activation in addition to Tbx6.
source: On the other hand, mouse Ripply2 requires Mesp2 for transcriptional activation in addition to Tbx6 (Dunty et al., 2008; Morimoto et al., 2007), and suppresses Mesp2 function through destabilization of Tbx6.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Dunty et al., 2008 and Morimoto et al., 2007.

claim: Ripply factors are not completely functionally conserved within vertebrates.
source: However, there is no evidence of a similar repression mechanism in mice, and we suggested the negative regulation in mouse to be mediated by the destabilization of T-box proteins (Oginuma et al., 2008; Zhao et al., 2015), arguing that Ripply factors are not completely functionally conserved within vertebrates.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Ripply functions differ between zebrafish/Xenopus and mice.

claim: The Tbx6 expression domain was elongated by one-somite-length with MG132 treatment for 2 hr in vivo.
source: This result is in agreement with the in vivo discovery that the Tbx6 expression domain was elongated by one-somite-length with MG132 treatment for 2 hr (Oginuma et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study by Oginuma et al., 2008.

claim: Tbx6Δ124~152aa has no transcriptional activity.
source: As Tbx6Δ124-152aa-venus has no transcriptional activity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), we selected ES clones in which Tbx6-venus was heterozygously knocked-in and an endogenous Tbx6 allele was intact for chimera production (Tbx6Tbx6(Δ124-152aa)-venus/+).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.
